title: Decisions With More Than One Condition
content:
What problem does this solve?
Many decisions depend on several facts at once. and, or, and not let you combine True-or-False conditions into one rule.

Build the rule in plain language first
and means every connected requirement must be True. or means at least one connected condition must be True. not reverses one Boolean value.

Small examples
  True and False  -> False
  False or True   -> True
  not True        -> False

Translate before typing
If the rule says 'a guide AND enough supplies AND no warning,' write those three facts separately first. Then connect them. Parentheses are useful when a rule mixes and/or and you want the grouping to be obvious.

Vocabulary after the behavior
A Boolean value is True or False. Boolean logic combines or reverses these values.
concepts: and requires all connected conditions to be True
or requires at least one connected condition to be True
Translate the English rule into separate conditions before combining them

examples.title: Both required
examples.code:
has_key = True
code_correct = False
print(has_key and code_correct)
examples.explanation: One requirement is False, so the combined result is False.

examples.title: Either route
examples.code:
north_open = False
south_open = True
print(north_open or south_open)
examples.explanation: One open route is enough, so the result is True.

examples.title: Departure rule
examples.code:
has_guide = True
supplies = 12
warning_active = False
print(has_guide and supplies >= 10 and not warning_active)
examples.explanation: All three requirements pass, including the reversed warning flag.

common_mistakes: Using or when every requirement must pass
Using and when any one danger should be enough
Comparing Boolean variables to the strings "True" or "False"
Writing a chained comparison such as supplies >= 10 and <= 20 instead of repeating the value
Ignoring grouping when and/or are mixed

exercises.title: Both must be true
exercises.code_to_predict:
a = True
b = False
print(a and b)
hints: and checks whether both sides are True.
b is False, so the pair cannot be True.
The output is False.

exercises.title: Choose and
exercises.prompt: A door opens only when the key is present AND the code is correct. Which operator expresses that rule?
hints: The word only means both requirements must pass.
Choose the operator that requires every connected condition to be True.
The operator is and.
exercises.success_message: Correct. Both requirements must pass together.

exercises.title: Either one is enough
exercises.code_to_predict:
north_open = False
south_open = True
print(north_open or south_open)
hints: or asks whether at least one side is True.
south_open is True even though north_open is False.
The output is True.

exercises.title: Choose or
exercises.prompt: Any one danger should trigger a warning: flooding, a broken bridge, or poor visibility. Which operator belongs between the danger checks?
hints: A single danger is enough.
Choose the operator that becomes True when at least one condition is True.
The operator is or.
exercises.success_message: Right. One active danger is enough to trigger the warning.

exercises.title: Reverse a flag
hints: Start with warning_active = True.
not reverses the Boolean value.
not True becomes False.

exercises.title: Trace the full rule
exercises.prompt: What prints? Evaluate each requirement separately first.
exercises.code_to_predict:
has_guide = True
supplies = 12
warning_active = True
if has_guide and supplies >= 10 and not warning_active:
    print("Depart")
else:
    print("Wait")
hints: Evaluate has_guide, supplies >= 10, and not warning_active separately.
The first two are True, but warning_active is True, so not warning_active is False.
and needs every part True, so the else branch prints Wait.

exercises.title: False clearance
exercises.prompt: Both a guide and at least 10 supplies are required. Change only the Boolean operator so the starter values produce False.
exercises.starter_code:
has_guide = False
supplies = 12
can_depart = has_guide or supplies >= 10
print(can_depart)
exercises.reference_solution:
has_guide = False
supplies = 12
can_depart = has_guide and supplies >= 10
print(can_depart)
hints: The current rule becomes True when either requirement passes.
The policy says both facts are required at the same time.
Replace or with and.

tests.message: Use and because both requirements are required.

exercises.title: Departure clearance
exercises.prompt: Using the supplied variables, assign a Boolean variable named can_depart. It must be True only when a guide is present, supplies are at least 10, and no warning is active. Then print can_depart.
exercises.starter_code:
has_guide = True
supplies = 12
warning_active = False

# Assign can_depart, then print it
exercises.reference_solution:
has_guide = True
supplies = 12
warning_active = False
can_depart = has_guide and supplies >= 10 and not warning_active
print(can_depart)
hints: Write the three requirements separately in your head first.
Connect the guide and supply requirements with and. Reverse warning_active with not.
Use can_depart = has_guide and supplies >= 10 and not warning_active.
exercises.success_message: The Boolean value now represents the whole departure rule in one reusable result.

exercises.title: Route Clearance Board
exercises.prompt:
Use the supplied variables to choose exactly one status.

Rules in order:
1. Denied if warning_active OR route_damaged.
2. Otherwise Cleared if has_guide AND supplies >= 10.
3. Otherwise Review.

Print exactly: Status: <status> using an f-string. After it passes, manually try these scenarios: supply boundary 10, no guide, active warning, and damaged route.
exercises.starter_code:
has_guide = True
supplies = 10
warning_active = False
route_damaged = False

# Choose status, then print one formatted line
exercises.reference_solution:
has_guide = True
supplies = 10
warning_active = False
route_damaged = False

if warning_active or route_damaged:
    status = "Denied"
elif has_guide and supplies >= 10:
    status = "Cleared"
else:
    status = "Review"

print(f"Status: {status}")
hints: Handle blockers first because either danger should deny the route regardless of supplies.
Use or for the two blockers, then elif with and for guide plus supply clearance.
Shape: if warning_active or route_damaged -> Denied; elif has_guide and supplies >= 10 -> Cleared; else -> Review; then print status with an f-string.
exercises.success_message: The board now combines blockers, requirements, an ordered branch chain, and formatted output.
